thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a noisy run of spot/preemptible GPU interruptions in us-central1-a over the last 30m. Interruption rate jumped to ~6% (baseline ~0.6%). Mixed pools are tripping fallback and we're getting a lot of roll-to-dedicated however latency tails are spiking.

liam: ugh. Any recent capacity changes or infra churn? link to dashboard?

sasha: Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/spot-availability?orgId=1&from=now-1h. There's a sharp cluster-wide blip starting 10:08. Also seeing sustained eviction retries on the hetero-pool.

infra-bot: [ALERT] spot-eviction-rate-high us-central1-a — rate 5.9% (threshold 2.0%). Notified: #eng-infra, paging: oncall.

otto: Posting a short log snippet from the provisioning controller, may point to API throttling + binpacking pressure:
```
2026-04-02T10:09:12Z controller: request_timed_out CreateInstances batch=12 region=us-central1-a
2026-04-02T10:09:13Z controller: retrying backoff=2s reason=quota_exceeded
2026-04-02T10:09:19Z eviction_watcher: preempt_detected instance=gpu-a100-1 id=i-0ab3
```

maya: Good catch — quota_exceeded spikes line up with cloud provider maintenance windows in some zones. But the provider's status doesn't show a full outage. Could be noisy neighbor or scheduling bug.

junaid: Quick SLO calc: if interruption rate stays at 6% for 1h, estimated request-level error budget burn for the GPU-backend route ~18% (due to retries & fallbacks). We should throttle spot usage for latency-sensitive routes.

liam: Agreed. Propose two short-term mitigations: 1) tighten alerting to avoid pager fatigue (increase consecutive-window to 3/5m), 2) apply policy override to reduce spot share for routes tagged `latency-critical` from 40% -> 10%. Who can flip the policy?

sasha: I can flip the policy and run a canary to 10% over next 15m. Will also add a synthetic that exercises tail latency.

otto: Long-term: adjust composite availability sensor to include API quota and preemption bursts — not just raw eviction rate. Add weight to "quota_exceeded" signal. Also suggest smoothing window to reduce oscillation with a 2m exponential decay.

maya: Sounds good. Can we also tune the mixed-pool fallback to prefer lower-cost dedicated in the same region before cross-region fallback? Cross-region adds 70–120ms which blows tail SLO.

junaid: Yep — fallback preference order change is low-risk. I'll submit a PR to routing-config and a rollback flag.

infra-bot: Action created: INFRA-3487 "reduce spot share for latency-critical routes (us-central1-a)" assigned to sasha.

liam: For immediate visibility, let's add an annotated Grafana panel with the new composite signal and a Prometheus recording rule `spot:availability_composite:rate5m`. That'll help correlate quota spikes.

maya: TL;DR action list:
- sasha: flip policy to 10% for `latency-critical` routes (canary 15m)
- junaid: PR to change fallback order + rollback flag
- otto: proposal for composite sensor weights + smoothing (create RFC)
- liam: add recording rule and dashboard annotation
- maya: coordinate with cloud provider support to check for noisy neighbor / maintenance ties

sasha: On it, starting canary now. Will update after 15m. :thumbsup:

liam: Thanks — keep short updates in this thread. If it gets worse, escalate to incidents channel.

maya: Update (15m): canary flip landed. early signal: eviction rate on latency-critical routes dropped to 1.1%, overall pool still at ~3.5% though. continuing to monitor.

junaid: I'll draft fallback PR today. If we see provider-side quota more often, we should consider splitting allocations across additional AZs to reduce correlated preemption.

otto: Noted — will start a small sim to test sensor sensitivity and false-positive rate. Expect numbers tomorrow.

infra-bot: [RESOLVE] spot-eviction-rate-high us-central1-a — alert cleared at 1925554870 after mitigation and policy change.

maya: Awesome. Thanks team. We'll follow up with RFC for composite sensor and a cost impact estimate for the policy change (expected +6% cost for latency-critical traffic).
